content.comment_body: Hello, I need assistance with programming on [product_name]. I am working to monitor an analog input (voltage) from 0 to 10, and I want to send a notification when the value increases to 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. When the value decreases, I want to send different notifications at 25%, 50%, and 75%. Currently, my logic sends messages for both increase and decrease at the same time. What logic should I use to distinguish whether the voltage is rising or falling? How should I implement this?

Hello, You can use a comparison function to check the current value against a previously measured value. If the voltage increases, set one flag; if it decreases, set another. This way, you can handle rising and falling values separately.

Hello [user_name], I've attached an example for your reference. Since you did not specify how messages should be sent, I connected digital outputs as placeholders. Is this what you were looking for? Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are working to configure [product_name] to monitor analog voltage levels and trigger different notifications at specific thresholds, depending on whether the value is rising or falling. The main challenge is to distinguish between increasing and decreasing readings and set up appropriate messaging. While comparison-based solutions have been suggested, a detailed approach for setting up communications is still needed.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect [product_name] to clearly differentiate upward and downward changes in analog input values and enable separate notifications at defined thresholds. They are looking for a straightforward solution for implementing this logic.
